 SECTION TWO: CLOZE TEST {10 MKS}
2. Read the passage below and fill in the black spaces with appropriate words.
 Road …………………………on our highways have become a major source of worry in the
 country.…………………… does a day…………. without an accident being reported. Statistics from the
 …………………department indicate that there is an ………………increase in the number of accidents,
 reported per day.
 Quite often, a number of innocent people have ended up losing their lives. These…………… are often victims
 of …………………..drivers who don’t seem to care much for the welfare of their……………………..Most
 of these drivers, when tested with Alco-blow have been found to be………………..the influence
 of…………………. It is with this in mind that we expect the law enforcement officers not to relent in their
 crackdown on such errant drivers.

3. Read the poem below and answer questions that follow:
 THE NIGHT MAIL
 This is the Night Mail crossing the boarder
 Bringing the cheque and the postal order,
 Letters for the rich, fetters for the poor,
 The shop at the corner, the girl next door.
 Pulling up the Beatlock, a steady climb
@2020
 “The gradient’s against her, but she is on time”
 Past cotton grass and moorland boulder
 Shoveling white steam over her shoulder
 Snorting noisily, she passes
 Silent miles of wind bent grass.

5. Shouting and screaming from your class disrupted the other students during study time. As the class monitor,
 you have been called by the teacher on duty to her office to give an explanation complete the conversation
 below by filling in the blank spaces. (8mks)
 TEACHER: You are the class monitor of Form Two East, aren’t you?
 YOU……………………………………………………………………………………………….
 ……………………………………………………………………………………………………..
 …………………………………………………………………………………………………….(lmk)
 TEACHER: Why was your class shouting and screaming?
 YOU: l am not sure, madam. The noise started at the back of the classroom.
 TEACHER:……………………………………………………………………………………….(1mk)
 YOU: You see madam; I sit at the front of the classroom and by the time I turned to look, the boys at the back
 were already on top of the desks and some were trying to jump out of the window.
 TEACHER :………………………………………………………………………………………(lmk)
 YOU: I ran out, madam!
 TEACHER:………………………………………………………………………………………(lmk)
 YOU: I am sorry madam, but it seemed like there was great danger in the middle of the class. I had to run for
 my life.
 TEACHER: When the noise subsided what did you find out?
 YOU:…………………………………………………………………………………………… (1mk)
 TEACHER: A snake?
 YOU:……………………………………………………………………………………………(lmk)
 TEACHER: Whose toy snake was it?
 YOU:……………………………………………………………………………………..…….. (1mk)
 TEACHER: You can go now, but I still need to know whose toy snake it was.
 YOU:…………………………………………………………………………………………. (lmk)
